title: Long TBT — Warsh Sintra Hawkishness + 10Y at 4.50% Ceiling: Rate Path ETF
entry: Long TBT $34.50–$36.50 at July 2 open (TBT at $35.50, corresponding to TLT ~$86.40 July 1 close). Entry is most efficient on the open before NFP (8:30 AM ET) prints — if NFP is hot, TBT gaps up 5–8% immediately on the 10Y spike; if NFP is soft, TBT dips to $33–34 providing a better entry for the structural Warsh hike thesis. Both entry windows are valid but the pre-NFP entry captures the optionality of a hot print with smaller size risk. Do NOT enter above $38 — above that level the 10Y has already moved to ~4.65% and the near-term risk/reward compresses. Size 2% of gross. This is a low-conviction structural rate-path trade, not an NFP directional bet.
stop_loss: TBT daily close below $32.00 — implies TLT has rallied above $91 (10Y falling below 4.15%), which would occur only if: (1) NFP prints below 80K today, triggering recession-fear flight-to-quality; (2) Warsh explicitly reverses his Sintra hawkish signal at the July 16 FOMC press conference, confirming a hold and signaling September rate cut; or (3) a significant geopolitical de-escalation (Iran second ceasefire, Ukraine deal) drives a global risk-off-into-Treasuries bid that overwhelms the domestic rate-hike thesis. Below $32, the rate compression scenario has definitively reasserted and TBT's 2x leverage creates accelerating loss; exit immediately.
targets: $39.00 — 10Y tests 4.65% as NFP today prints above 140K and Warsh July hike probability reaches 45%; TBT gains 9.9% from $35.50 entry; cover 40% of position on 10Y closing above 4.60%
$43.00 — BofA three-hike path confirmed: Warsh July 16 statement explicitly signals a move; 10Y reaches 4.80%; TBT gains 21.1%; cover 40%
$48.00 — 10Y approaches 5.00%, 30Y clears 5.20%; Warsh July hike executed on July 16 and September hike begins pricing; TBT gains 35.2%; exit final 20%
catalyst: Governor Warsh's appearance at the ECB Sintra Forum (June 25–27, 2026) is the primary catalyst shift. Warsh's prepared remarks and Q&A explicitly introduced the possibility of a July 2026 rate hike contingent on continued above-trend labor market data — a material departure from the prior post-Versailles ceasefire framework that had assumed a Q4 2026 first hike at earliest. The market moved from 8% to 33% July hike probability overnight. Today's NFP binary (consensus 114K; Warsh's apparent threshold is ~130K+) is the key data point that either validates or temporarily delays this thesis. TBT (ProShares UltraShort 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF) provides 2x leveraged inverse exposure to TLT — when the 10Y rises (TLT falls), TBT rises at approximately 2x the TLT move. At 10Y = 4.50% heading into NFP, TBT is positioned at the inflection where even a small upward rate move produces meaningful ETF gains.
thesis:
This trade is the structural rate-path expression of the Warsh July hike thesis, distinct from the existing long-TLT-nfp-weak-print-hedge position. The two positions are complementary, not contradictory: TLT long is a short-term hedge for a soft NFP outcome (1–2 week holding period, defined by today's data); TBT long is the medium-term expression of the structural hike path that persists regardless of today's single data point (3–6 week holding period, defined by the July 16 FOMC decision and September expectations).

The Warsh Sintra signal is the most significant central bank communication event since the April FOMC shock. Warsh has never been known for ambiguity — when a Federal Reserve Governor explicitly raises the prospect of an imminent hike at an international central bank forum, the market has historically been right to take that signal seriously. The move from 8% to 33% July hike probability in 48 hours is the market partially catching up to a signal the bond market has been pricing since the BofA three-hike framework emerged in mid-June.

The 10Y at 4.47–4.50% represents a critical technical level. For the past three weeks, the 10Y has tested 4.50% and been unable to sustain a close above it — held back by ceasefire-driven risk appetite compression in yields. With the ceasefire premium now partially absorbed, the 10Y has no structural anchor below 4.50% if the Warsh July hike materializes. The next resistance is 4.65% (the BofA 3-hike base case fair value), and TBT would gain approximately 10% from current levels if 10Y reaches 4.65%.

TBT is not a buy-and-hold instrument — it suffers from volatility drag (decay) in a whipsaw market. The trade must have a defined exit: either (1) Warsh July hike is fully priced by July 15 (exit before the FOMC event), or (2) Warsh July 16 explicitly hikes (exit into the hike on the event), or (3) the hike thesis breaks (stop at $32 on TLT rally). Holding TBT through a choppy 3-6 week period without the thesis resolving is the primary risk — the leverage magnifies decay costs.

The counter-party argues: (1) the Warsh Sintra remarks were interpreted hawkishly by markets but were deliberately ambiguous — he said 'data-dependent' not 'I will hike in July'; (2) a single weak NFP today would immediately compress the July hike probability back to 8–10%, killing the TBT thesis; (3) TBT's expense ratio and daily reset mechanism create structural drag that requires the rate move to happen quickly (within weeks) to produce the modeled returns. These risks are precisely why conviction is low and size is 2%.
bull_case: NFP today prints 158K with wages +0.33% — above Warsh's apparent threshold. 10Y spikes from 4.50% to 4.62% on the July 2 session. TBT closes July 2 at $38.50 (+8.5%). The week of July 7–11, Warsh follows up with a WSJ interview (the Fed's traditional pre-FOMC communication channel) explicitly signaling a July hike. 10Y reaches 4.80% by July 15. TBT exits at $43 (Target 2) the week before the July 16 FOMC. Return: +21.1% on 2% position = +0.42% gross.
bear_case: NFP today prints 88K — below the soft-landing corridor floor. Warsh July hike probability collapses from 33% to 10%. Flight-to-quality bid hits TLT; 10Y falls from 4.50% to 4.25%. TBT falls from $35.50 to $33.50 intraday (-5.6%). The TLT long position (separate) captures this scenario and partially offsets. TBT does not stop out at $32 but spends 2 weeks bleeding via volatility drag as the market debates whether the Warsh signal was misinterpreted. Exit TBT at $32 stop if the structural thesis fails to reassert within 3 weeks.
invalidation: TBT daily close below $32.00 (10Y falls below 4.15%); OR Warsh July 16 FOMC vote is a hold (not a hike) and post-meeting statement removes July hike language explicitly; OR NFP today prints below 80K (recession signal — flight to Treasuries overwhelms the hawkish rate path); OR 10Y falls below 4.20% on two consecutive weekly closes (structural bond rally confirming rate-cut cycle resumes)
